title: AAPCS (ARM Architecture Procedure Call Standard)
summary: AAPCS is the standard calling convention for ARM (32-bit and 64-bit). AArch64: integer args in x0-x7 (first 8), float args in v0-v7, return in x0/v0. Callee-saved: x19-x28, x29 (FP), x30 (LR). AArch32: r0-r3 (args), r0-r1 (return), r4-r11 (callee-saved), r12 (IP), r13 (SP), r14 (LR), r15 (PC). Stack: 8-byte aligned (AArch32) or 16-byte aligned (AArch64).

structure.meaning: Integer return in x0 (and x1 for 128-bit). Float return in v0.
x19-x28, x29 (FP), x30 (LR). x0-x18 are caller-saved.
Integer return in r0 (and r1 for 64-bit). Float return in s0/d0.

notes: AAPCS is the standard for ARM Linux, Android, and iOS.
AArch64 (ARM 64-bit) uses x0-x7 for args (vs 6 for x86-64).
AArch64 has 31 general-purpose registers (vs 16 for x86-64).
Link register (LR/x30) holds the return address (not on stack by default).
Frame pointer (FP/x29) is optional in AArch64 (can be omitted for leaf functions).
